p3.rule: The label is the triage nurse's Emergency Severity Index at an emergency department visit (MIMIC-IV-ED). ESI 1 means immediate life-saving intervention; ESI 2 high-risk, confused, lethargic, severe pain or distress, or unstable vital signs; ESI 3 two or more resources expected; ESI 4 one resource; ESI 5 none. In this department most visits are ESI 3, and ESI 5 is almost never assigned.

i1.rule: The label is the length of the inpatient stay that followed this admission, from the actual encounter period: '1 day or less', '2 to 3 days', '4 to 7 days', 'more than 7 days'. Only admission-time information is shown. Stays of 2 to 7 days are the most common; stays of one day or less are rare.

i2.rule: The label is the ICD-10-GM chapter of the single principal diagnosis that was coded for billing (DRG) at the end of this stay, mapped by code range: chapter II (C00-D48) includes benign and uncertain neoplasms D10-D48; chapter III starts at D50; chapter VII is the eye (H00-H59) and chapter VIII the ear (H60-H95); chapter XIX covers injuries and poisoning (S00-T98). Neoplasms (II) and circulatory diseases (IX) together make up over half of the stays.

i3.rule: The label is the ICD-O-3 behaviour digit of the pathologist's coded conclusion for this report: behaviour /3 (malignant, primary), /6 (metastatic) and /9 count as malignant; /0 (benign), /1 (uncertain) and /2 (in situ) count as not malignant. 'Metastatic' is asked only for malignant reports and means behaviour /6. Most coded reports in this archive are malignant.
